sanskrit: tataḥ śokābhisaṃtaptaṃ sugrīvaṃ klinnavāsanam śākhāmṛgamahāmātrāḥ parivāryopatasthire
english: Then the great ministers among the tree-dwelling monkeys gathered around Sugrīva, who was burning with grief and whose garments were still damp.

sanskrit: abhigamya mahābāhuṃ rāmam akliṣṭakāriṇam sthitāḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve pitāmaham ivarṣayaḥ
english: All of them approached the mighty-armed Rāma, who acts without fatigue, and stood with folded hands, like sages before Brahmā the Grandfather.

sanskrit: tataḥ kāñcanaśailābhas taruṇārkanibhānanaḥ abravīt prāñjalir vākyaṃ hanumān mārutātmajaḥ
english: Then Hanūmān, son of the Wind-god, who shines like a mountain of gold and whose face blazes like the rising sun, spoke these words with folded hands.

sanskrit: bhavatprasādāt sugrīvaḥ pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mahat vānarāṇāṃ suduṣprāpaṃ prāpto rājyam idaṃ prabho
english: "By your grace, O lord, Sugrīva has obtained this great kingdom of the monkeys — the realm of his fathers and grandfathers — which was so very difficult to recover."

sanskrit: bhavatā samanujñātaḥ praviśya nagaraṃ śubham saṃvidhāsyati kāryāṇi sarvāṇi sasuhṛjjanaḥ
english: "With your permission he will enter the fair city and attend to all the affairs of state together with his friends and allies."

sanskrit: snāto 'yaṃ vividhair gandhair auṣadhaiś ca yathāvidhi arcayiṣyati ratnaiś ca mālyaiś ca tvāṃ viśeṣataḥ
english: "Having bathed and been anointed with various perfumes and medicinal herbs according to prescribed rite, he will especially honour you with jewels and garlands."

sanskrit: imāṃ giriguhāṃ ramyām abhigantum ito 'rhasi kuruṣva svāmi saṃbandhaṃ vānarān saṃpraharṣayan
english: "You should come from here to this lovely mountain cave, O master; establish your connection with us and delight the monkeys."

sanskrit: evam ukto hanumatā rāghavaḥ paravīrahā pratyuvāca hanūmantaṃ buddhimān vākyakovidaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Hanūmān, the wise Rāghava, slayer of enemy heroes, who was skilled in speech, replied to Hanūmān.

sanskrit: caturdaśasamāḥ saumya grāmaṃ vā yadi vā puram na pravekṣyāmi hanuman pitur nirdeśapālakaḥ
english: "For fourteen years, dear friend, I shall not enter any village or city — I who honour my father's command, O Hanūmān."

sanskrit: susamṛddhāṃ guhāṃ divyāṃ sugrīvo vānararṣabhaḥ praviṣṭo vidhivad vīraḥ kṣipraṃ rājye 'bhiṣicyatām
english: "Let the heroic Sugrīva, bull among monkeys, who has entered the richly furnished and splendid cave according to rite, be swiftly consecrated to the kingdom."

sanskrit: evam uktvā hanūmantaṃ rāmaḥ sugrīvam abravīt imam apy aṅgadaṃ vīra yauvarājye 'bhiṣecaya
english: Having spoken thus to Hanūmān, Rāma said to Sugrīva: "O hero, consecrate this Aṅgada also as crown prince."

sanskrit: pūrvo 'yaṃ vārṣiko māsaḥ śrāvaṇaḥ salilāgamaḥ pravṛttāḥ saumya catvāro māsā vārṣikasaṃjñitāḥ
english: "This is the first month of the rainy season, Śrāvaṇa, that brings the coming of the waters; the four months known as the rainy season have now begun, dear friend."

sanskrit: nāyam udyogasamayaḥ praviśa tvaṃ purīṃ śubhām asmin vatsyāmy ahaṃ saumya parvate sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
english: "This is not the season for military exertion. Enter your fair city; I shall dwell on this mountain together with Lakṣmaṇa, dear friend."

sanskrit: iyaṃ giriguhā ramyā viśālā yuktamārutā prabhūtasalilā saumya prabhūtakamalotpalā
english: "This mountain cave is lovely and spacious, well-ventilated, rich in water, and abundantly filled with lotuses and blue water-lilies, dear friend."

sanskrit: kārtike samanuprāpte tvaṃ rāvaṇavadhe yata eṣa naḥ samayaḥ saumya praviśa tvaṃ svam ālayam abhiṣiñcasva rājye ca suhṛdaḥ saṃpraharṣaya
english: "When Kārtika arrives, devote yourself to the slaying of Rāvaṇa — this is our agreement, dear friend. Enter your own dwelling, get yourself consecrated to the kingdom, and gladden your friends."

sanskrit: iti rāmābhyanujñātaḥ sugrīvo vānararṣabhaḥ praviveśa purīṃ ramyāṃ kiṣkindhāṃ vālipālitām
english: Thus granted leave by Rāma, Sugrīva, bull among monkeys, entered the fair city of Kiṣkindhā, which had been governed by Vālin.

sanskrit: taṃ vānarasahasrāṇi praviṣṭaṃ vānareśvaram abhivādya prahṛṣṭāni sarvataḥ paryavārayan
english: Thousands of monkeys, filled with joy, saluted that lord of monkeys as he entered and surrounded him on all sides.

sanskrit: tataḥ prakṛtayaḥ sarvā dṛṣṭvā harigaṇeśvaram praṇamya mūrdhnā patitā vasudhāyāṃ samāhitāḥ
english: Then all the subjects, upon seeing the lord of the monkey host, prostrated themselves with bowed heads to the ground with composed minds.

sanskrit: sugrīvaḥ prakṛtīḥ sarvāḥ saṃbhāṣyotthāpya vīryavān bhrātur antaḥpuraṃ saumyaṃ praviveśa mahābalaḥ
english: The valiant and mighty Sugrīva addressed all the subjects, raised them up, and then entered the fair inner apartments of his brother.

sanskrit: praviśya tv abhiniṣkrāntaṃ sugrīvaṃ vānararṣabham abhyaṣiñcanta suhṛdaḥ sahasrākṣam ivāmarāḥ
english: When Sugrīva, bull among monkeys, had entered and then came forth again, his friends consecrated him just as the immortals consecrated the Thousand-eyed Indra.

sanskrit: tasya pāṇḍuram ājahruś chatraṃ hemapariṣkṛtam śukle ca bālavyajane hemadaṇḍe yaśaskare
english: They brought for him a white parasol adorned with gold, and two white fly-whisks with golden handles that bestow glory.

sanskrit: tathā sarvāṇi ratnāni sarvabījauṣadhāni ca sakṣīrāṇāṃ ca vṛkṣāṇāṃ prarohān kusumāni ca
english: Likewise all manner of jewels, all kinds of seed-bearing plants and medicinal herbs, and the sprouts and blossoms of milk-bearing trees.

sanskrit: śuklāni caiva vastrāṇi śvetaṃ caivānulepanam sugandhīni ca mālyāni sthalajāny ambujāni ca
english: And white garments, white unguent, fragrant garlands, and flowers both of land and water.

sanskrit: candanāni ca divyāni gandhāṃś ca vividhān bahūn akṣataṃ jātarūpaṃ ca priyaṅgumadhusarpiṣī
english: And divine sandalwood and many various fragrances, whole unhusked grain, gold, priyaṅgu grain, honey, and clarified butter.

sanskrit: dadhicarma ca vaiyāghraṃ vārāhī cāpy upānahau samālambhanam ādāya rocanāṃ samanaḥśilām ājagmus tatra muditā varāḥ kanyās tu ṣoḍaśa
english: And curd, a tiger-skin, and sandals made from the hide of a boar. Sixteen choice maidens arrived there with joy, bearing an anointing preparation, yellow orpiment, and manaḥśilā mineral.

sanskrit: tatas te vānaraśreṣṭhaṃ yathākālaṃ yathāvidhi ratnair vastraiś ca bhakṣyaiś ca toṣayitvā dvijarṣabhān
english: Then they satisfied the best of the twice-born with jewels, garments, and food-offerings as befitting the time and proper rite, doing honour to that foremost of monkeys.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuśaparistīrṇaṃ samiddhaṃ jātavedasaṃ mantrapūtena haviṣā hutvā mantravido janāḥ
english: Then those versed in sacred formulas, having laid out a spread of kuśa grass and kindled the fire of Jātavedas, offered oblations into it with clarified butter consecrated by mantras.

sanskrit: tato hemapratiṣṭhāne varāstaraṇasaṃvṛte prāsādaśikhare ramye citramālyopaśobhite
english: Then, on the lovely summit of the palace that was furnished with a golden throne-platform covered with choice spreads and adorned with colourful garlands,

sanskrit: prāṅmukhaṃ vividhair mantraiḥ sthāpayitvā varāsane nadīnadebhyaḥ saṃhṛtya tīrthebhyaś ca samantataḥ
english: having placed him facing east on an excellent seat with various mantras, and having gathered water from all directions — from rivers, streams, and sacred fords —

sanskrit: āhṛtya ca samudrebhyaḥ sarvebhyo vānararṣabhāḥ apaḥ kanakakumbheṣu nidhāya vimalāḥ śubhāḥ
english: — and having brought water from all the oceans and stored the pure and auspicious water in golden vessels, the bulls among monkeys —

sanskrit: śubhair vṛṣabhaśṛṅgaiś ca kalaśaiś cāpi kāñcanaiḥ śāstradṛṣṭena vidhinā maharṣivihitena ca
english: — using auspicious bull-horns and golden vessels, according to the rite prescribed by the scriptures and established by the great sages —

sanskrit: gajo gavākṣo gavayaḥ śarabho gandhamādanaḥ maindaś ca dvividaś caiva hanūmāñ jāmbavān nalaḥ
english: — Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Śarabha, Gandhamādana, Mainda, Dvivida, Hanūmān, Jāmbavān, and Nala —

sanskrit: abhyaṣiñcanta sugrīvaṃ prasannena sugandhinā salilena sahasrākṣaṃ vasavo vāsavaṃ yathā
english: — consecrated Sugrīva with clear and fragrant water, just as the Vasus consecrated Vāsava, the Thousand-eyed Indra.

sanskrit: abhiṣikte tu sugrīve sarve vānarapuṃgavāḥ pracukruśur mahātmāno hṛṣṭās tatra sahasraśaḥ
english: When Sugrīva had been consecrated, all those noble bulls among monkeys there raised a shout of joy in their thousands.

sanskrit: rāmasya tu vacaḥ kurvan sugrīvo haripuṃgavaḥ aṅgadaṃ saṃpariṣvajya yauvarājye 'bhiṣecayat
english: Acting upon Rāma's word, Sugrīva, the foremost among the tawny monkeys, embraced Aṅgada and consecrated him as crown prince.

sanskrit: aṅgade cābhiṣikte tu sānukrośāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ sādhu sādhv iti sugrīvaṃ mahātmāno 'bhyapūjayan
english: When Aṅgada too had been consecrated, the noble and compassionate monkeys honoured Sugrīva, saying "Well done, well done!"

sanskrit: hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākīrṇā patākādhvajaśobhitā babhūva nagarī ramyā kṣikindhā girigahvare
english: The fair city of Kiṣkindhā in its mountain gorge was filled with joyful and prosperous people and shone with banners and flags.

sanskrit: nivedya rāmāya tadā mahātmane mahābhiṣekaṃ kapivāhinīpatiḥ rumāṃ ca bhāryāṃ pratilabhya vīryavān avāpa rājyaṃ tridaśādhipo yathā
english: Having reported the great consecration to the noble Rāma, the valiant lord of the monkey army, having also recovered his wife Rumā, obtained the kingdom just as the lord of the thirty gods.

sanskrit: abhiṣikte tu sugrīve praviṣṭe vānare guhām ājagāma saha bhrātrā rāmaḥ prasravaṇaṃ girim
english: When Sugrīva had been consecrated and the monkey had entered the cave, Rāma came together with his brother to Mount Prasravaṇa.

sanskrit: śārdūlamṛgasaṃghuṣṭaṃ siṃhair bhīmaravair vṛtam nānāgulmalatāgūḍhaṃ bahupādapasaṃkulam
english: That mountain resounded with tigers and deer, was thronged with lions of fearsome roar, was dense with various shrubs and creepers, and was thick with many trees.

sanskrit: ṛkṣavānaragopucchair mārjāraiś ca niṣevitam megharāśinibhaṃ śailaṃ nityaṃ śucijalāśrayam
english: Frequented by bears, monkeys, and langurs, and by wild cats, that mountain resembling a mass of clouds always sheltered pure water.

sanskrit: tasya śailasya śikhare mahatīm āyatāṃ guhām pratyagṛhṇata vāsārthaṃ rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha
english: On the summit of that mountain, Rāma together with Saumitri took up for dwelling a great and spacious cave.

sanskrit: avasat tatra dharmātmā rāghavaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ bahudṛśyadarīkuñje tasmin prasravaṇe girau
english: The righteous Rāghava dwelt there together with Lakṣmaṇa on that Mount Prasravaṇa, full of ravines and glades offering many lovely views.

sanskrit: susukhe 'pi bahudravye tasmin hi dharaṇīdhare vasatas tasya rāmasya ratir alpāpi nābhavat hṛtāṃ hi bhāryāṃ smarataḥ prāṇebhyo 'pi garīyasīm
english: Even though that mountain was most pleasant and rich in many things, dwelling there afforded not the slightest joy to Rāma, who constantly thought of the wife who had been taken from him — she who was dearer than life itself.

sanskrit: udayābhyuditaṃ dṛṣṭvā śaśāṅkaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ āviveśa na taṃ nidrā niśāsu śayanaṃ gatam
english: Especially upon seeing the moon risen at its rising, sleep would not come to him at night even when he had lain down.

sanskrit: tat samutthena śokena bāṣpopahatacetasaṃ taṃ śocamānaṃ kākutsthaṃ nityaṃ śokaparāyaṇam tulyaduḥkho 'bravīd bhrātā lakṣmaṇo 'nunayan vacaḥ
english: His brother Lakṣmaṇa, sharing in his pain, spoke consoling words to that scion of Kākutstha, whose mind was shattered by tears, who constantly lamented with grief arising from this sorrow, ever given over to grief.

sanskrit: alaṃ vīra vyathāṃ gatvā na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi śocato hy avasīdanti sarvārthā viditaṃ hi te
english: "Enough, hero — do not surrender to anguish; you should not grieve. For you well know that all one's purposes sink when one grieves."

sanskrit: bhavān kriyāparo loke bhavān devaparāyaṇaḥ āstiko dharmaśīlaś ca vyavasāyī ca rāghava
english: "You, Rāghava, are foremost in action in the world; you are devoted to the gods; you are a believer; you are of righteous disposition; and you are a man of resolution."

sanskrit: na hy avyavasitaḥ śatruṃ rākṣasaṃ taṃ viśeṣataḥ samarthas tvaṃ raṇe hantuṃ vikramair jihmakāriṇam
english: "For without firm resolve, you are not capable of slaying in battle that enemy, that Rākṣasa in particular — that one who acts crookedly — with your valour."

sanskrit: samunmūlaya śokaṃ tvaṃ vyavasāyaṃ sthiraṃ kuru tataḥ saparivāraṃ taṃ nirmūlaṃ kuru rākṣasaṃ
english: "Uproot your grief, make your resolve firm, and then extirpate that Rākṣasa together with his entire retinue."

sanskrit: pṛthivīm api kākutstha sasāgaravanācalām parivartayituṃ śaktaḥ kim aṅga puna rāvaṇam
english: "O scion of Kākutstha, you are capable of overturning the entire earth with its oceans, forests, and mountains — how much less, then, Rāvaṇa?"

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu khalu te vīryaṃ prasuptaṃ pratibodhaye dīptair āhutibhiḥ kāle bhasmac channam ivānalam
english: "I, for my part, am awakening your heroic energy that has fallen asleep, as one revives with blazing oblations a fire covered in ashes at the right moment."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇasya tu tad vākyaṃ pratipūjya hitaṃ śubham rāghavaḥ suhṛdaṃ snigdham idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having honoured Lakṣmaṇa's beneficial and auspicious words, Rāghava spoke this reply to his loving friend.

sanskrit: vācyaṃ yad anuraktena snigdhena ca hitena ca satyavikrama yuktena tad uktaṃ lakṣmaṇa tvayā
english: "What should be said by one who is devoted, affectionate, and well-wishing — by one endowed with true valour — that have you said, O Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: eṣa śokaḥ parityaktaḥ sarvakāryāvasādakaḥ vikrameṣv apratihataṃ tejaḥ protsāhayāmy aham
english: "This grief, which depresses all one's purposes, is hereby abandoned. I rouse my energy, which is unhindered in its valorous deeds."

sanskrit: śaratkālaṃ pratīkṣe 'ham iyaṃ prāvṛḍ upasthitā tataḥ sarāṣṭraṃ sagaṇaṃ rākṣasaṃ taṃ nihanmy aham
english: "I await the season of autumn — this rainy season has now arrived. When it passes, I shall slay that Rākṣasa together with his kingdom and his entire host."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā hṛṣṭo rāmasya lakṣmaṇaḥ punar evābravīd vākyaṃ saumitrir mitranandanaḥ
english: Hearing those words of Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā and the joy of his friends, was delighted and spoke once more.

sanskrit: etat te sadṛśaṃ vākyam uktaṃ śatrunibarhaṇa idānīm asi kākutstha prakṛtiṃ svām upāgataḥ
english: "This speech you have uttered is worthy of you, O destroyer of enemies. Now, O scion of Kākutstha, you have returned to your true nature."

sanskrit: vijñāya hy ātmano vīryaṃ tathyaṃ bhavitum arhasi etat sadṛśam uktaṃ te śrutasyābhijanasya ca
english: "Having understood your own true heroic power, you ought to be as you really are. What you have said is befitting both your learning and your noble lineage."

sanskrit: tasmāt puruṣaśārdūla cintayañ śatrunigraham varṣārātram anuprāptam atikrāmaya rāghava
english: "Therefore, O tiger among men, let the night of the rainy season that has arrived pass by while you contemplate the subduing of the enemy, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: niyamya kopaṃ pratipālyatāṃ śarat kṣamasva māsāṃś caturo mayā saha vasācale 'smin mṛgarājasevite saṃvardhayañ śatruvadhe samudyataḥ
english: "Restraining your anger, await the autumn season. Bear with these four months; dwell on this mountain with me — this mountain frequented by the king of beasts — growing ever more resolved for the slaughter of the enemy."

sanskrit: sa tadā vālinaṃ hatvā sugrīvam abhiṣicya ca vasan mālyavataḥ pṛṣṭhe rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt
english: Then Rāma, having slain Vālin and consecrated Sugrīva and now dwelling on the slopes of Mount Mālyavat, spoke to Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa kālaḥ saṃprāptaḥ samayo 'dya jalāgamaḥ saṃpaśya tvaṃ nabho meghaiḥ saṃvṛtaṃ girisaṃnibhaiḥ
english: "This season has now arrived — the time of the coming of waters. Look now at the sky covered over with clouds like mountains."

sanskrit: nava māsa dhṛtaṃ garbhaṃ bhāskārasya gabhastibhiḥ pītvā rasaṃ samudrāṇāṃ dyauḥ prasūte rasāyanam
english: "Having drunk up the essence of the oceans through the rays of the sun and held it as an embryo for nine months, the sky now gives birth to its elixir."

sanskrit: śakyam ambaram āruhya meghasopānapaṅktibhiḥ kuṭajārjunamālābhir alaṃkartuṃ divākaram
english: "One could climb up into the sky by staircases formed of clouds and deck the sun himself with garlands of Kuṭaja and Arjuna blossoms."

sanskrit: saṃdhyārāgotthitais tāmrair anteṣv adhikapāṇḍuraiḥ snigdhair abhrapaṭacchadair baddhavraṇam ivāmbaram
english: "With its smooth cloud-coverings that are copper-coloured from the crimson of twilight at the edges and more pale in the middle, the sky looks as if a wound has been bound up."

sanskrit: mandamārutaniḥśvāsaṃ saṃdhyācandanarañjitam āpāṇḍujaladaṃ bhāti kāmāturam ivāmbaram
english: "With its gentle-wind sighs, painted with the sandal-paste of twilight glow, bearing clouds that are somewhat pale, the sky shines like one smitten with longing."

sanskrit: eṣā dharmaparikliṣṭā navavāripariplutā sīteva śokasaṃtaptā mahī bāṣpaṃ vimuñcati
english: "This earth, afflicted by the law of nature, inundated with fresh water, and tormented by grief — like Sītā — sheds its tears."

sanskrit: meghodaravinirmuktāḥ kahlārasukhaśītalāḥ śakyam añjalibhiḥ pātuṃ vātāḥ ketakigandhinaḥ
english: "The breezes released from the bellies of clouds, cool and pleasant as the Kahlāra water-lily, fragrant with the scent of Ketaka — one could drink them up in cupped hands."

sanskrit: eṣa phullārjunaḥ śailaḥ ketakair adhivāsitaḥ sugrīva iva śāntārir dhārābhir abhiṣicyate
english: "This mountain with its Arjuna trees in full bloom, fragrant with Ketaka flowers, is consecrated by the streams of rain — like Sugrīva, his enemies now at peace."

sanskrit: meghakṛṣṇājinadharā dhārāyajñopavītinaḥ mārutāpūritaguhāḥ prādhītā iva parvatāḥ
english: "Wearing dark cloud-skins, with their sacred threads of downward streams, their caves filled with wind-sound, the mountains are like those who have thoroughly studied the Vedas."

sanskrit: kaśābhir iva haimībhiḥ vidyudbhir iva tāḍitam antaḥstanitanirghoṣaṃ savedanam ivāmbaram
english: "Struck as if by golden whips — by lightning bolts — with the rumble of thunder deep within, the sky seems to be in pain."

sanskrit: nīlameghāśritā vidyut sphurantī pratibhāti me sphurantī rāvaṇasyāṅke vaidehīva tapasvinī
english: "The lightning flashing among the dark clouds appears to me like the suffering Vaidehī, writhing in Rāvaṇa's embrace."

sanskrit: imās tā manmathavatāṃ hitāḥ pratihatā diśaḥ anuliptā iva ghanair naṣṭagrahaniśākarāḥ
english: "These directions, which were beneficial to those struck by the arrows of Manmatha, are now obscured — smeared over as it were by the clouds, with their stars and moon invisible."

sanskrit: kva cid bāṣpābhisaṃruddhān varṣāgamasamutsukān kuṭajān paśya saumitre puṣṭitān girisānuṣu mama śokābhibhūtasya kāmasaṃdīpanān sthitān
english: "Look, O Saumitri, at the Kuṭaja shrubs in bloom here and there on the mountain slopes — pent up with moisture like tears, exuberant at the arrival of the rains — they stand there kindling desire in me who am already overwhelmed by grief."

sanskrit: rajaḥ praśāntaṃ sahimo 'dya vāyur nidāghadoṣaprasarāḥ praśāntāḥ sthitā hi yātrā vasudhādhipānāṃ pravāsino yānti narāḥ svadeśān
english: "The dust is settled, the wind today carries moisture, the afflictions spreading from the summer heat have abated. Military campaigns of kings have halted; wanderers and travellers return to their own lands."

sanskrit: saṃprasthitā mānasavāsalubdhāḥ priyānvitāḥ saṃprati cakravākaḥ abhīkṣṇavarṣodakavikṣateṣu yānāni mārgeṣu na saṃpatanti
english: "The Cakravāka birds, eager to reach their beloved Mānasa lake, set out now together with their mates; but their vehicles do not run on the roads battered by the constant rain-water."

sanskrit: kva cit prakāśaṃ kva cid aprakāśaṃ nabhaḥ prakīrṇāmbudharaṃ vibhāti kva cit kva cit parvatasaṃniruddhaṃ rūpaṃ yathā śāntamahārṇavasya
english: "The sky adorned with scattered clouds shines bright in some places and dark in others, its form obstructed here and there by mountains — like the great ocean when it has grown calm."

sanskrit: vyāmiśritaṃ sarjakadambapuṣpair navaṃ jalaṃ parvatadhātutāmram mayūrakekābhir anuprayātaṃ śailāpagāḥ śīghrataraṃ vahanti
english: "The mountain rivers carry swiftly water mingled with the blossoms of Sarja and Kadamba trees, copper-coloured from the mountain minerals, followed by the cries of peacocks."

sanskrit: rasākulaṃ ṣaṭpadasaṃnikāśaṃ prabhujyate jambuphalaṃ prakāmam anekavarṣaṃ pavanāvadhūtaṃ bhūmau pataty āmraphalaṃ vipakvam
english: "The Jambū fruit, full of juice and resembling a bee in colour, is being relished abundantly; and the mango fruit, ripened fully, is tossed down to the ground by the wind."

sanskrit: vidyutpatākābhir alaṃkṛtānām udīrṇagambhīramahāravāṇām vibhānti rūpāṇi balāhakānāṃ raṇodyatānām iva vāraṇānām
english: "The forms of the clouds adorned with lightning-banners, emitting deep and mighty sounds, shine like great war-elephants poised for battle."

sanskrit: meghābhikāmī parisaṃpatantī saṃmoditā bhāti balākapaṅktiḥ vātāvadhūtā varapauṇḍarīkī lambeva mālā racitāmbarasya
english: "A row of cranes flying all about, eager toward the clouds and joyful, shaken by the wind, shines like a garland of choice white lotuses hung in the sky."

sanskrit: nidrā śanaiḥ keśavam abhyupaiti drutaṃ nadī sāgaram abhyupaiti hṛṣṭā balākā ghanam abhyupaiti kāntā sakāmā priyam abhyupaiti
english: "Sleep approaches Keśava slowly; the river rushes swiftly to the ocean; the joyful crane approaches a cloud; the ardent beloved approaches her lover."

sanskrit: jātā vanāntāḥ śikhisupranṛttā jātāḥ kadambāḥ sakadambaśākhāḥ jātā vṛṣā goṣu samānakāmā jātā mahī sasyavanābhirāmā
english: "Forest borders have come alive, with peacocks dancing beautifully; Kadamba trees have grown, with Kadamba-laden boughs; bulls have grown ardent among the cows, equally desirous; the earth has become lovely, adorned with fields of grain and groves."

sanskrit: vahanti varṣanti nadanti bhānti dhyāyanti nṛtyanti samāśvasanti nadyo ghanā mattagajā vanāntāḥ priyāvinīhāḥ śikhinaḥ plavaṃgāḥ
english: "Rivers flow; clouds rain; rutting elephants trumpet; forest borders gleam; devoted-to-beloved women meditate; peacocks dance; monkeys take breath."

sanskrit: praharṣitāḥ ketakapuṣpagandham āghrāya hṛṣṭā vananirjhareṣu prapāta śabdākulitā gajendrāḥ sārdhaṃ mayūraiḥ samadā nadanti
english: "Thrilled, having caught the fragrance of Ketaka blossoms, the great elephants in the forest waterfalls, disturbed by the thunderous sounds, cry out together with the maddened peacocks."

sanskrit: dhārānipātair abhihanyamānāḥ kadambaśākhāsu vilambamānāḥ kṣaṇārjitaṃ puṣparasāvagāḍhaṃ śanair madaṃ ṣaṭcaraṇās tyajanti
english: "Bees, beaten by the downpours of rain and hanging on Kadamba boughs, slowly relinquish the intoxication that was quickly gained from being immersed in the flowers' nectar."

sanskrit: aṅgāracūrṇotkarasaṃnikāśaiḥ phalaiḥ suparyāpta rasaiḥ samṛddhaiḥ jambūdrumāṇāṃ pravibhānti śākhā nilīyamānā iva ṣaṭpadaughaiḥ
english: "The boughs of the Jambū trees shine out with their fruits resembling heaped coal-powder, richly filled with abundant juice, as if settled upon by swarms of bees."

sanskrit: taḍitpatākābhir alaṃkṛtānām udīrṇagambhīramahāravāṇām vibhānti rūpāṇi balāhakānāṃ raṇodyatānām iva vāraṇānām
english: "The forms of the storm-clouds adorned with lightning-banners, emitting deep and mighty rising sounds, shine like elephants roused for battle."

sanskrit: mārgānugaḥ śailavanānusārī saṃprasthito megharavaṃ niśamya yuddhābhikāmaḥ pratināgaśaṅkī matto gajendraḥ pratisaṃnivṛttaḥ
english: "A maddened king elephant, walking the path and following the mountain forest, having set out and then heard the thunderclap of the clouds, eager for battle and suspecting it to be a rival bull, has turned back."

sanskrit: muktāsakāśaṃ salilaṃ patad vai sunirmalaṃ patrapuṭeṣu lagnam hṛṣṭā vivarṇacchadanā vihaṃgāḥ surendradattaṃ tṛṣitāḥ pibanti
english: "Birds with ruffled plumage, joyful and thirsty, drink from the folds of leaves the water falling like pearls — pure and clear, gifted by the lord of the gods."

sanskrit: nīleṣu nīlā navavāripūrṇā megheṣu meghāḥ pravibhānti saktāḥ davāgnidagdheṣu davāgnidagdhāḥ śaileṣu śailā iva baddhamūlāḥ
english: "Clouds — dark, filled with fresh water — shine clinging to dark clouds, and mountains scorched by forest-fire cling to mountains scorched by forest-fire, as if fixed in place by roots."

sanskrit: mattā gajendrā muditā gavendrā vaneṣu viśrāntatarā mṛgendrāḥ ramyā nagendrā nibhṛtā nagendrāḥ prakrīḍito vāridharaiḥ surendraḥ
english: "The great elephants are in rut; the chief bulls are joyful; in the forests the lions rest at greater ease; the great trees are lovely; the great serpents are still; and Indra, lord of the gods, plays with the rain-bearing clouds."

sanskrit: vṛttā yātrā narendrāṇāṃ senā pratinivartate vairāṇi caiva mārgāś ca salilena samīkṛtāḥ
english: "The military campaigns of kings have ceased; armies turn back; enmities and roads alike are levelled by water."

sanskrit: māsi prauṣṭhapade brahma brāhmaṇānāṃ vivakṣatām ayam adhyāyasamayaḥ sāmagānām upasthitaḥ
english: "In the month of Prauṣṭhapada, the sacred season has arrived — the time of study of the Brahman — for brāhmaṇas who wish to expound, and for those who chant the Sāmaveda."

sanskrit: nivṛttakarmāyatano nūnaṃ saṃcitasaṃcayaḥ āṣāḍhīm abhyupagato bharataḥ koṣakādhipaḥ
english: "Bharata, the guardian of the royal treasury, having now finished his seasonal observances and accumulated his stores, has surely observed the Āṣāḍhī vow."

sanskrit: nūnam āpūryamāṇāyāḥ sarayvā vadhate rayaḥ māṃ samīkṣya samāyāntam ayodhyāyā iva svanaḥ
english: "Surely the current of the swelling Sarayū river rises stronger — like the sound of Ayodhyā seeing me come home."

sanskrit: imāḥ sphītaguṇā varṣāḥ sugrīvaḥ sukham aśnute vijitāriḥ sadāraś ca rājye mahati ca sthitaḥ
english: "These rains, full of abundance, Sugrīva enjoys in happiness — his enemy defeated, his wife restored to him, established in a great kingdom."

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu hṛtadāraś ca rājyāc ca mahataś cyutaḥ nadīkūlam iva klinnam avasīdāmi lakṣmaṇa
english: "But I, my wife stolen and fallen from a great kingdom, sink down, O Lakṣmaṇa, like a waterlogged riverbank."

sanskrit: śokaś ca mama vistīrṇo varṣāś ca bhṛśadurgamāḥ rāvaṇaś ca mahāñ śatrur apāraṃ pratibhāti me
english: "My grief is vast, the rains make travel utterly impossible, and Rāvaṇa is a great enemy — the obstacle before me seems without end."

sanskrit: ayātrāṃ caiva dṛṣṭvemāṃ mārgāṃś ca bhṛśadurgamān praṇate caiva sugrīve na mayā kiṃ cid īritam
english: "Seeing this season unfit for marching and the roads utterly impassable, and since Sugrīva bows before me, I have said nothing at all to him."

sanskrit: api cātiparikliṣṭaṃ cirād dāraiḥ samāgatam ātmakāryagarīyastvād vaktuṃ necchāmi vānaram
english: "Moreover, the monkey has been long distressed and has only recently been reunited with his wives; because my own need weighs heavily on me, I do not wish to press him."

sanskrit: svayam eva hi viśramya jñātvā kālam upāgatam upakāraṃ ca sugrīvo vetsyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: "For Sugrīva will himself, having rested and knowing that the proper time has come, recognise the obligation of repaying a service — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: tasmāt kālapratīkṣo 'haṃ sthito 'smi śubhalakṣaṇa sugrīvasya nadīnāṃ ca prasādam anupālayan
english: "Therefore I stand here awaiting the right moment, O auspicious one, watching for the clearing of Sugrīva and of the rivers."

sanskrit: upakāreṇa vīro hi pratikāreṇa yujyate akṛtajño 'pratikṛto hanti sattvavatāṃ manaḥ
english: "A hero is indeed bound by service rendered to return service; an ungrateful one who does not repay wounds the hearts of those who are virtuous."

sanskrit: athaivam uktaḥ praṇidhāya lakṣmaṇaḥ kṛtāñjalis tat pratipūjya bhāṣitam uvāca rāmaṃ svabhirāma darśanaṃ pradarśayan darśanam ātmanaḥ śubham
english: Then, thus addressed, Lakṣmaṇa listened carefully, joined his palms in reverence, honoured that speech, and spoke to Rāma — displaying his own auspicious outlook to him whose very sight is beautiful.

sanskrit: yathoktam etat tava sarvam īpsitaṃ narendra kartā nacirād dharīśvaraḥ śaratpratīkṣaḥ kṣamatām imaṃ bhavāñ jalaprapātaṃ ripunigrahe dhṛtaḥ
english: "All that you have desired as you have spoken it, the lord of the monkeys will accomplish before long. Awaiting the autumn, may you, O king of men, bear this outpour of rain, firm in your resolve to subdue the enemy."
